The '''Star Wars CCG aftermarket''' is the secondary market for [[Decipher]]'s Star Wars Customizable Card Game: singles, sealed product, misprints, and promotional items bought and sold after release. Decipher's Star Wars license ended in 2001. The remaining stock was then sold off at heavy discounts, and the supply of Decipher-era cards and promotional items has been fixed since.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], starwarsccg.org (2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]</ref> According to Decipher CEO Warren Holland, customers had bought nearly $250 million of SWCCG product by 2002.<ref name="encyc" />

== Sealed product ==
=== Booster packs and starter decks ===
Decipher sold booster packs in display boxes and, for some sets, 60-card starter decks. Pack size, price, and box count changed over the game's life. <ref name="encyc" />

Oct 2026 prices are PriceCharting eBay sold prices (with sale date) where available, otherwise a store's listed price read 13 October 2026.<ref name="boxcalc">Calculated as packs per box × booster MSRP, both from the Collecting Encyclopedia; no Decipher box price was found.</ref> In Endor packs a foil replaces the rare in about 1 in 9 packs.<ref name="encyc" />

Early 12-pack [[Enhanced Premiere]] boxes were not split evenly among the six premium cards, so [[Leia With Blaster Rifle]] and [[Han With Heavy Blaster Pistol]] were short prints. Later evenly split boxes carry a "#414 Custom Display" sticker on the bottom.<ref name="encyc" /> Some Enhanced Jabba's Palace cards ended up in Star Trek CCG ''The Trouble with Tribbles'' packs because of a packaging-plant error. Decipher replaced the packs when customers returned the cards.<ref name="encyc" />

After the license ended, third parties bundled leftover packs into retail boxes; see [[Unofficial repackaged products]]. Leftover factory trays of commons, including a Cloud City Light Side commons tray, reached the secondary market.<ref name="hills-tray">[https://wholesalegaming.com/starwars/ Star Wars Card Games Products], Hill's Wholesale Gaming (Cloud City Light Side Commons Factory Tray). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260523161214/https://wholesalegaming.com/starwars/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Rarity ==
''Main article: [[Rarity]]''

Rarity was printed as a letter (C, U, R) plus an optional number that set how often a card appeared on its print sheet. On the Premiere rare sheet, each R1 appears twice and each R2 four times, so an R1 is half as common as an R2.<ref name="encyc" /> Other rarities include F (fixed, starter-deck cards) and XR (the exclusive rares in Death Star II starter decks). UR marks [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]]'s two ultra rares, [[Luke Skywalker, Jedi Knight]] and [[Emperor Palpatine]].<ref name="encyc" />

Foils came in several forms:
* [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] had an 18-card foil subset.<ref name="encyc" />
* The [[Reflections]] sets were all-foil chase sets. Reflections has 87 very rare, 25 super rare, and 2 ultra rare foils (Darth Vader and Luke Skywalker). On its foil sheets an ultra rare appears once, a super rare twice, and a very rare four times.<ref name="encyc" />
* Tatooine, Coruscant, and Theed Palace added [[Alternate Image]] (AI) rares. On the Tatooine rare sheet each rare appears eight times, and two of those eight are the AI version for cards that have one.<ref name="encyc" />
* Promotional foils, 28 in all, were foil copies of earlier cards given out at tournaments and as purchase incentives (2000–2002). Each tournament gave one to the winner and one to a random player; a new card rotated in each month and stayed in use for two months.<ref name="encyc" />

Collation could change real scarcity. Japanese Hoth rare sheets were collated 3 Light Side to 1 Dark Side, so Dark Side rares from that set are harder to find.<ref name="encyc" />

== Misprints and production errors ==
Cards with a corrected version:<ref name="encyc" />
* [[R-3PO]] (Hoth) showed the image of [[K-3PO (Kay-Threepio)|K-3PO]]. Decipher swapped returned copies for a shrink-wrapped corrected card; it said 110,000 wrong copies were printed and that returned cards would be destroyed.
* [[Dodge]] (Cloud City) appeared four times on its common sheet, once with the last word "free" missing.
* [[Asteroid Sanctuary]] (Dagobah) was reprinted with errata, by mail and in ''Scrye'' 4.4 (November 1997).
* [[Electrobinoculars]] and [[Tatooine: Lars' Moisture Farm]] in the Premiere Introductory Two-Player Game had incorrect game text.
* [[Eriadu]] in early Jedi Packs had a white dot where the dot should be red.
* [[Turn It Off! Turn It Off!]] (Hoth): some copies have an extra "0" after the lore's closing quote.

Production errors that are not separate card versions include blank cards, "Premiere Blue" cards, roller-mark embossing on some Death Star II sheets, and miscuts. Blank cards come in six known front and back combinations, from Hoth on; "Premiere Blue" cards were tinted by dried-up yellow ink.<ref name="encyc" /> A Hoth test run printed the 27 Light Side rares with Dark Side backs. It was never released, but single cards and uncut sheets reached the secondary market through former employees.<ref name="encyc" />

== Notable collectibles ==
* '''[[SWCCG Memorabilia#Lucasfilm and executive items|Executive Gift Set]]''' (2001): about 250 boxed sets, each holding almost two complete sets of Premiere Limited, made as gifts for Lucasfilm and Decipher executives. Most were never given out, and they reached the secondary market after the license ended.<ref name="encyc" />
* '''Oversized cards''': 5×7-inch versions of [[Aurra Sing (AI)]] and two Mara Jade cards were Decipher Store gifts for orders over $20. Reflections boxes had 5×7 objective box toppers.<ref name="encyc" />
* '''Box and case toppers''': Reflections II had four foil box toppers and a Japanese Darth Vader foil case topper.<ref name="encyc" />

== Pricing history ==
Late sets are worth the most, not early ones. The last Decipher sets had smaller print runs, while early sets were printed heavily.<ref name="potomac" /><ref name="qs2020" />
* '''2009:''' a distributor restocked [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] booster boxes at $294 and called the set the hardest of the Reflections sets to find. It said Theed Palace and Coruscant were also very hard to find.<ref name="potomac">[http://blog.potomacdist.com/2009/08/spotlight-on-tough-to-find-restocks.html Spotlight On Tough-To-Find Restocks], Potomac Distribution blog (19 August 2009). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260419201602/http://blog.potomacdist.com/2009/08/spotlight-on-tough-to-find-restocks.html Internet Archive]</ref> ''Death Star II'' was then one of the more expensive sets to buy.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192945/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''2020:''' sealed SWCCG product sold on eBay at prices a ''Quiet Speculation'' writer found surprising, and ten loose booster packs sold for $47.<ref name="qs2020">Sigmund Ausfresser, [https://www.quietspeculation.com/2020/05/surprising-value-in-old-collectible-card-games/ Surprising Value in Old Collectible Card Games], Quiet Speculation (4 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261013174018/https://www.quietspeculation.com/2020/05/surprising-value-in-old-collectible-card-games/ Internet Archive]</ref> By December, sealed product was "selling for never-before-seen prices".<ref name="qs2020b">[https://www.quietspeculation.com/2020/12/asset-explosion-an-economic-analysis/ Asset Explosion: An Economic Analysis], Quiet Speculation (December 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260527084926/https://www.quietspeculation.com/2020/12/asset-explosion-an-economic-analysis/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''2021:''' booster boxes sold for at least $500 and up to more than $2,000, and a top non-foil card went for about $300 on eBay.<ref name="vgc">Morgan Lewis, [https://vgculturehq.com/the-resurgence-of-star-wars-ccg/ The Resurgence of Star Wars CCG], VGCultureHQ (19 August 2021). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260518145903/https://vgculturehq.com/the-resurgence-of-star-wars-ccg/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''2024:''' hobbyDB ranked AI and foil singles among the ten most valuable Star Wars trading cards in its database, alongside Topps cards. One was [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo (AI)]] ($340).<ref name="hobbydb">[https://blog.hobbydb.com/2024/06/21/10-valuable-star-wars-trading-cards-topps-decipher/ 10 Valuable Star Wars Trading Cards From Topps, Decipher and More], hobbyDB blog (21 June 2024). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20240719130002/https://blog.hobbydb.com/2024/06/21/10-valuable-star-wars-trading-cards-topps-decipher/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''2025–2026:''' sealed [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] booster boxes (30 packs, $3.29 MSRP each) sold on eBay for $1,676 to $3,200. Sealed [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] boxes (60 packs, $2.50 each) sold for $255 to $449.<ref name="pccor">[https://www.pricecharting.com/game/star-wars-ccg-coruscant/booster-box Booster Box Prices: Star Wars CCG Coruscant], PriceCharting (eBay sold listings, viewed 13 October 2026). Snapshot: [https://swccg.com/snapshots/prices/star-wars-ccg-coruscant-booster-box.html swccg.com]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261013204730/https://swccg.com/snapshots/prices/star-wars-ccg-coruscant-booster-box.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pccc">[https://www.pricecharting.com/game/star-wars-ccg-cloud-city/booster-box Booster Box Prices: Star Wars CCG Cloud City], PriceCharting (eBay sold listings, viewed 13 October 2026).
